To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The Kaldi toolkit has been extended to support neural-based LM training.

1) we describe an extension to Kaldi that supports recurrent neural network language models; 2) we describe a method for using letter-based features and importance sampling in neural network language modeling; 3) we describe a new objective function for training neural network language models that allows for training unnormalized probabilities; 4) we describe a way to combine letter-based features and one-hot encoding in neural network language models to allow for handling large vocabularies; and 5) our experiments show

1) the use of letter-based features is beneficial for language model performance, 2) the use of one-hot encoding is beneficial for handling large vocabularies, and 3) importance sampling is a useful method for training large-vocabulary language models with recurrent neural networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How do we train neural networks to model language? Can we use neural networks to model the structure of language, in the way that n-grams do?
the development of a neural network based language model for automatic speech recognition (Kaldi-RNNLM).
the problem of language model adaptation for the task of automatic speech recognition.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kaldi toolkit can serve as a general framework for language modeling, and that it can be used to develop state-of-the-art neural network models.
Kaldi-RNLLM provides a flexible toolkit that can be used for training and decoding of neural-based language models.

Kaldi-RNLLM can be used as a drop-in replacement for Kaldi’s existing language modeling tools, and that it can be used with a variety of different language model architectures, including the Kaldi ngram language model, the Kaldi factored ngram language model and the Kaldi RNNLM.
